rulings.evidence: Nixtamalized corn flour used as the chili's thickener - not cornmeal, not corn starch, not wheat flour. Board reports no commodity and no capture match and no vocabulary row shares a core word, so it goes to the registrar. 1/4 cup = 30 g.

'Drained and rinsed' from a 15 oz. tin is canned usage, so the canned row is the SAME form and not a flip - the identical call as 'black beans' -> canned-black-beans on 2026-08-26. Board 7 of 7; weighed at the same 15 oz basis the settled kidney-bean line uses.

A topping the source never quantified, so optional, per the 'Sliced onions' -> onions precedent. Reuses the same vocabulary row this batch used for healthy-hamburger-helper; REFUSED fat-free-cheddar, which is a different product and price class. Weighed at a nominal 14 g per serving.
Wedges are a cut, not a food, and the board carries limes at 5 of 7, cheapest 0.25 at Walmart - a reuse. Unquantified garnish, so optional; weighed at 1 1/2 limes for the source's 6 servings.

An unquantified either/or serving suggestion naming TWO different foods, and the estate's standing rejection forbids collapsing corn chips into tortilla-chips, so there is no single food to cost. The board's `tortillas` match is soft flour tortillas, a wrong food. Dropped as a garnish rather than costed against a guess; the chili is complete without it.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Nixtamalized corn flour (Maseca and store equivalents), its own SKU in the Hispanic-foods aisle. It is not corn flour proper, not cornmeal, not corn starch and not any flour id: the lime treatment changes the food, the price and the use, and the board reports no commodity and no capture match while no vocabulary row shares a core word with it. Nothing on the board prices a nixtamalized corn product under another spelling, so this is a genuinely new food rather than a rename.
